title: Minimal sideband backchannel protocol and canary failure contract
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Define and accept a minimal, auditable sideband/backchannel protocol for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that permits limited, authenticated outbound or inbound communication strictly for: (1) telemetry heartbeat (health/upgrade progress), (2) canary coordination and automated rollback triggers during staged upgrades, and (3) operator-initiated emergency fetch of critical artifacts. The protocol must preserve air-gapped compatibility where customers opt out, provide clear allowed ports and host patterns, and enumerate failure/rollback contracts for staged rollouts.
goals: Provide a compact protocol specification that operators can evaluate for regulatory air-gap constraints
Ensure canary rollouts have deterministic failure detection signals and automated rollback contracts
Minimize attack surface and data leakage; only allow structured, minimal telemetry and signed artifact metadata
Offer testable acceptance criteria and a reproducible test harness for customers and Redwood QA
scope: Protocol spec (message shapes, auth, endpoints, retry semantics, sideband vs primary paths)
Acceptance criteria for canary failure detection and automated rollback thresholds
Operational runbook snippets (diagnostics, forced rollback, emergency artifact fetch)
Pass/fail test cases to validate behavior in partitioned/intermittent-egress scenarios
out_of_scope: Designing new primary data-plane network tunnels for model traffic
Extensive change to existing operator UI beyond a single toggle and status indicators
Full PKI rollout for customer-managed CAs (we will support mTLS using customer-provided certs but not supply a CA)
acceptance_criteria: Spec published: single-page protocol doc with message examples (JSON), required headers, and authentication modes
Minimum-viable sideband modes: (A) outbound heartbeat-only with mTLS, (B) inbound ephemeral fetch via customer-allowed proxy with signed requests
Canary failure contract: if 5% of nodes report scoring regression > 2x baseline or 3 consecutive error-class X responses in 10 minutes, rollout must auto-pause and shift traffic to baseline variant
Network contract: required egress ports (TCP 443) and optional management port (TCP 8443) documented; host allowlist patterns clearly specified; zero-entropy payloads for telemetry (no customer PII)
Authentication: mTLS required for operators+Redwood control-plane; client certs rotateable via documented TTL; fallback token mode allowed only for airgap lab-mode with explicit customer approval

Telemetry payloads limited to enumerated fields: node_id, component, timestamp, health_code, canary_score_delta, image_sha (artifact provenance). No raw prompts, embeddings, or customer payload allowed
Test harness: automated integration test that simulates (a) intermittent 80% packet loss, (b) symmetric 3000ms latency, (c) complete egress block; expected outcomes recorded and compared
Runbook: operations runbook with step-by-step rollback, including commands to force a safe image pin and drain canary nodes
Privacy & compliance signoff: Security team review completed and documented as a link in the ticket
test_plan: Unit tests: validate message serialization and auth header validation
Integration: end-to-end canary scenario in staging with synthetic workloads and assertion on canary_score_delta metrics
Chaos tests: simulate network partitions and observe automated pause + rollback behavior
Fuzz tests: malformed messages, certificate expiry cases, and slow upstream responses
Customer-sim labs: run the harness in a sealed environment with a sample customer network policy and record mitigation time
rollout_strategy: Feature flag gated in Private control plane; default OFF
Beta customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks to validate real-world network variety
Canary pattern: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automated observations at each step
Automatic pause conditions and minimum-stable-time configuration documented (default 10m)
Fallback: immediate switch to pinned model variant and alert on-call with runbook link
dependencies: ENG-44122: operator mTLS certificate rotation support
ENG-44901: lightweight telemetry writer with field-level allowlist
SEC-1221: privacy review and data-flow diagram approval
DOCS-215: single-page protocol doc publication in Confluence
QA-807: test harness infra in staging
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers with strict no-egress policies will reject protocol. Mitigation: provide 'no-sideband' mode and an operator-run offline artifact injection path
Risk: accidental inclusion of sensitive payloads. Mitigation: transport-level and schema-level validators plus pre-release linter in CI
Risk: partial egress leading to split-brain canary signals. Mitigation: require quorum and multi-signal detection before auto-rollback
Risk: certificate expiry causing mass rollout pause. Mitigation: early warning telemetry and staggered rotation window in operator runbook
notes: Design trade-off: prefer minimal, auditable message shapes over richer telemetry to satisfy compliance teams
We explored a push vs pull model; chosen hybrid: outbound heartbeat push by default, inbound ephemeral fetch gated by explicit allowlist
Target audience: platform ops, security, and regulated customers running air-gapped or partially-connected sites
